alternatives_and_negative_results: Do not select external SDRAM or assert BRAM-only fit based only on aggregate bits; no memory-controller choice was approved.
applicability: AX309 RTL architecture and memory/buffering design.
assessed_root_cause: Actual memory feasibility depends on width/depth packing, dual-port demand, buffer lifetime, bank conflicts, arithmetic widths and temporary/debug storage.
author_role: historical project engineering record, backfilled by FPGA engineering copilot
chosen_corrective_method: Design explicit buffer lifetimes, access schedules and bank/port maps; estimate primitive count; then verify with ISE synthesis and implementation reports.
generalizable_lesson: Resource feasibility must be demonstrated at primitive and port level, then confirmed by synthesis and timing.
initial_faulty_assumption_or_design_deci: Three nominal buffers fitting under 72 KiB could be interpreted as proof that the radar chain fits the device.
non_applicability: Does not prove the proposed memory map will fit; board manual/resource report and actual ISE run are still required.
observable_consequence: S01 records the 576-Kbit BRAM and 16 DSP resource limits, explicitly labels raw capacity as a comparison only, and C02 leaves DSP/FF/BRAM/LUT/timing/throughput unmeasured.
observed_problem: The AX309 baseline has limited BRAM and DSP resources; a simple total-bit sum ignores primitive aspect ratios, ports, banking and simultaneous traffic.
repeatable_validation: Create a memory map and per-cycle port schedule; compare inferred BRAM primitives and utilization after synthesis.
reviewer_role: documentary evidence validation by FPGA engineering copilot; not a separate human reviewer
safety_contract_constraints: Board revision, ISE 14.7 availability and physical resource utilization remain unverified.
title: Raw BRAM bit capacity is not a memory architecture or fit result
